Tools
Walk tracker (GPS · opt-in)
Off. Tap Record to trace your path on foot — your phone will ask to use your location (choose While Using). Nothing is stored until you tap Save.
Session log
Start when you hit the rocks, end when you leave. Catches dated inside a session link to it automatically — log them on the spot or later that night.
Saved sessions: 0
Offline maps (beta)
Switch the base layer to Esri Sat, zoom to the area you want, then Save. Tiles for the current view (plus 2 zoom levels closer) are stored on this device so the map still draws with no signal. Imagery only — zones, spots & tides already work offline.
Depth points (your soundings)
shading opacity
Keeps the depth colours and lights the seabed from the NW — drop-offs and gutter walls show as bright/dark edges, flats stay even. Needs shading on.
Tints water by depth from your soundings — approximate; fades out where there's no data. With shading on, tap any shaded spot to read its estimated depth.
shade12 m
lines8 m
Dashed depth lines traced through your interpolated soundings — approximate, drawn only over water where you have data.
Measurement only — shows how long each pan rebuild takes, split by stage. Changes nothing on the map. Off by default; nothing is timed or stored while it's off.
Depth lines (traced / drawn / imported)
Only needed where no survey data is imported — the LiDAR shelf points already pin the shore along the covered coast.
Each Navionics route imports as one depth line. Name the route with its depth (e.g. "3" or "2.5m") and it auto-labels & colours; otherwise tap a line to set its depth.
Imported depths (LiDAR / survey CSV)
Depths must be metres below LAT (negative = dries). If your file is AHD heights, leave it — ask the build chat to convert. Offset is added to every depth on import. 0 points loaded across all regions.
Flats shading — tidal exposure, not depth. Brisbane River, Sunshine Coast and Moreton Bay / Redcliffe are topographic LiDAR (class-2 ground returns, no water penetration), so they paint fixed exposure bands and give no numeric readout. Bands are set from HAT — an astronomical-tide ceiling only: it excludes storm surge, barometric setup, and (Brisbane River especially) river flood stage. “Dries earliest” describes tide exposure — it is never a flood, depth or safety claim.
Zone legend (2024 plan)
Safety — crocodiles
Bargara sits south of Queensland's formal croc-country management area (it starts around the Boyne River near Gladstone), but vagrant crocodiles have been recorded further south — especially in rivers and creeks after floods. No natural waterway can be assumed crocodile-free.
Recent sightings (last 30 days) — QLD Gov dashboard
Report a sighting: QWildlife app or 1300 130 372 (option 1). Check the dashboard before fishing estuaries or creek mouths.
Backup (your data)
